text.p: Following are the main stories in Thursday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad said the government would do all it could to ensure the hostage-taking incident in Lima, Peru, where Malaysia's ambassador, Ahmad Mokhtar Selat, is one of the hostages, be resolved quickly.

- Mahathir said certain non-governmental organisations (NGOs) were purposely carrying out activities which could undermine the country and desscribed those behind them as traitors. The Prime Minister was commenting on the proposed move by nine NGOs to convene a "public tribunal" to discuss allegations of abuse of power by the police.

- Prime Minister Mahathir has not discounted the possibility of Malaysia making its own rockets one day, given the progress in its aerospace technology. He said the possibility was there as rocket parts now being made of composite materials in France for Arianspace could be manufactured in Malaysia.

- Prime Minister Mahathir warned that the Internal Security Act, which allows detention without trial, will be used if non-governmental organisations (NGOs) continue to bait the government. He said certain NGOs were prodding the government into taking action so that Malaysia's good name would be damaged.

- Malaysia's reserves are expected to increase by 19.1 percent to 41.2 percent of the gross domestic product (GDP) by the end of next year if Malaysians ensure the national savings campaign succeeds, Deputy Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said.
